title: Google to buy all output from largest US BESS under construction
gist: Google signed a PPA for all power from the first two phases of Cypress Creek's 1.6GW solar / 1.9GWh storage Steel River Energy Center in Arkansas, part of a wave of hyperscaler-backed BESS financing (including a $3.5bn debt package) that Benchmark frames as the fastest lever to meet AI-driven data centre power demand.

insights.claim: Google will purchase all power generated from the first two phases of Cypress Creek's Steel River Energy Center in Arkansas, a project combining 1.6GW of solar with 1.9GWh of battery storage.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: One of the largest solar-plus-storage PPAs tied directly to data centre load, signalling hyperscaler capital flowing at scale into grid-scale BESS.

insights.claim: A potential third phase of the Steel River project would raise its total battery storage capacity to 2.9GWh by 2029.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Signals a further expansion runway beyond the Google-backed phases, relevant for forecasting the project's long-run battery materials demand.

insights.claim: Power from the Steel River project flows to the grid via the utility Entergy Arkansas rather than directly to Google's facilities, offsetting load from existing and planned data centres nearby while meeting Google's clean power procurement needs through the power purchase agreement.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Illustrates the grid-connected (virtual) PPA structure hyperscalers use to green data centre load without direct interconnection — a template likely to recur across other US markets.
insights.locator: "Power will flow to the grid via the utility Entergy Arkansas..."

insights.claim: Deals like Google's Steel River PPA show data centre energy demand can drive renewable deployment at scale, but raise an open question about whether such builds meaningfully firm grid reliability broadly or primarily serve corporate decarbonisation commitments.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Investors in grid infrastructure should track whether hyperscaler-driven builds translate into broad grid resilience or stay narrowly corporate-serving, since that affects how utilities versus BESS developers should be valued.
insights.locator: "This deal demonstrates how data centre energy demand can drive renewable deployment..."

insights.claim: Pete Tillotson, a senior BESS analyst at Benchmark, said hyperscalers have historically looked to gas to power new load additions, but renewable PPAs like the Steel River deal demonstrate the growing relevance of clean power to the incoming wave of data centre capacity.
insights.speaker: Pete Tillotson, senior BESS analyst at Benchmark
insights.so_what: A direct analyst signal that clean-power PPAs are gaining share against gas peakers for new hyperscaler load — relevant for comparing gas versus renewable capex allocation among data centre operators.
insights.quote: While hyperscalers have historically looked to gas to power new load additions, renewable PPAs such as this demonstrate the relevance of clean power to the incoming wave of data centre capacity

insights.claim: BESS eases grid interconnection for large, inflexible new loads and is materially faster to deploy than gas peakers, nuclear, or transmission upgrades, a significant structural advantage given the pace of AI-driven data centre demand growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Frames battery storage as the fastest available lever to bring power online for AI load growth — a structural tailwind for BESS capex and the critical minerals feeding it.
insights.locator: "Deployment speed advantage amid AI demand growth"

insights.claim: The Steel River project's $3.5 billion in project financing was underwritten by Barclays, BNP Paribas, Santander, and Wells Fargo, demonstrating continued lender appetite for solar-paired storage despite the loss of federal tax credits and tariff volatility.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Bank financing at this scale despite policy headwinds is a bullish signal for continued capital availability in the US BESS sector.
insights.locator: "...the US$3.5 billion in project financing underwritten by Barclays, BNP Paribas, Santander, and Wells Fargo"

insights.claim: Of 29 grid-scale US energy projects tied to data centres tracked by Benchmark, Steel River ranks third largest by storage capacity, behind Sunstone Solar & Storage in Oregon (~7.2GWh) and the Pine Island data centre BESS in Minnesota (30GWh).
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Gives investors a ranked pipeline of the largest US data-centre-linked BESS projects to track for downstream lithium and nickel demand and financing flow.
insights.locator: "Of the 29 grid-scale energy projects in the US relating to data centres..."
